Closure.Name: Cummer Ave 45 m Northeast of C N R to 35 m Southwest of C N R
Closure.Description: Toronto-TMC: Rehabilitation work under Metrolinx contract IT-2024RTMD-766 for the bridge over Cummer Avenue. Scope of work includes installation of lumber against the edge of the bridge to facilitate waterproofing operation on the tracks. Equipment includes skid steer, boom lift, traffic barrels and signs. Alternating lane crossover will be completed by flagging traffic to one side of the pier (EB or WB) while the opposite side is closed for the operation. Bike lanes will be closed and bike will merge with traffic as per the traffic plan shown. One sidewalk will remain continuously closed to accommodate equipment & material storage and to support the operation during working hours.The other sidewalk to remain opened at all times. Pedestrians to be detoured from closed sidewalk to opened sidewalk at nearest crossings.

Closure.Name: Maxome Ave 1 m North of Finch Corridor Trl to 12 m South of Hepc
Closure.Description: Toronto-TMC: Drilling boreholes off-road in the grassy area next to the east outlet of Culvert ID. 733. The equipment and vehicles will be parked along the shoulder of Maxome Avenue in Toronto. The two (2) boreholes will be advanced to a depth of 6 m and 10 m. This is a geotechnical and environmental investigation to support the replacement of the failed armour stone walls at the downstream end of Culvert ID. 733. Drilling may take 1 - 2 days to complete for each borehole. Traffic control services will be used, and may be modified by traffic control specialist to better suit site conditions. Equipment to be used includes limited access drill rig, steel drums to store soil cuttings, drilling augers and rods.

Closure.Description:
Toronto-TMC: The construction of the New Etobicoke Civic Centre.
Multiplex Construction Canada will be managing the construction of the New Etobicoke Civic Centre Located at 3755 Bloor Street W. Etobicoke, Ontario M9A 1A2, located within the newly redeveloped Etobicoke Civic Centre Precinct (formerly the Westwood Theatre Lands).
The ECC is a mixed-use building comprising a wide range of community focused program and services. The building is arranged in a series of tall volumes towards the north, housing the municipal offices, while the lower floors towards the south contain all the public functions. It will also be compliant to the Toronto Accessibility Design Guidelines (TADG) to extend greater accessibility for all users.
With 508,000 square feet of accessible public-facing space, the new civic centre is the first of its kind to be built in the last 50 years and is designed as a state-of-the-art mixed-used civic hub that includes:
Civic Square • Approximately 47,000 sq

Toronto-TMC: - This project involves two sequential phases of underground utility work around Innis College on the University of Toronto St. George campus. The scope includes the installation of a chilled water system and a hydro duct bank, coordinated to avoid conflicts with existing and future infrastructure, as shown in the attached utility drawings.
Phase 1: - Location: bPNichol Lane (between Sussex Avenue and Lane South Bloor Street East, in the vicinity of Innis College). - Scope of Work: Installation of chilled water lines approximately 30 meters North of Sussex Avenue, including connections and terminations as per design drawings. The chilled water piping will be installed in a shared utility trench with consideration for future heating line installations by the University.

Closure.Description: Toronto-TMC: The Broadview and Eastern Flood Protection (BEFP) project will address flood vulnerability for urban land east of the Don River, between Eastern Avenue and rail corridor, the existing underpass at Eastern Avenue, and the proposed underpass at Broadview Avenue. As part of this construction, there will be utility relocations and reconstruction in this area, including city storm and sanitary sewers that run along Sunlight Park Rd. Buildings related to one business within the project footprint will be removed to allow for construction of the FPL and other necessary local infrastructure. The removal also enables future projects by others such as the Broadview Avenue Extension, East Harbour Transit Hub & Development and the Ontario Line.
